verdicts.target: TOTAL_COMPUTE zero_gap: MTP (multi-task pretraining) per-step signal amplification
verdicts.reason: MTP is live in stack (0.3 aux weight, 2 heads) but has no isolation receipt. The claim is that MTP bends FLOPs-to-target efficiency. No ablation comparing MTP-on vs MTP-off at same step/FLOPs budget. Even if small effect, it is quantifiable and currently unmeasured.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run two parallel 100-step rung-1 trainings (ff=16384, ~1.2B params): Treatment A with MTP enabled (aux_weight=0.3, 2 aux heads), Treatment B with MTP disabled (aux_weight=0). Hold all other hyperparams equal.
decisive_experiment.measurement: For each treatment: loss at step 100, FLOPs consumed (via torch.profiler), tokens-to-target-loss ratio. Compare: loss_100_A vs loss_100_B at same FLOPs budget. Check whether MTP reduced loss per FLOPs.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if MTP-off achieves lower loss_100 at same FLOPs, or if effect size is <2% loss improvement—indicating MTP is neutral or detrimental at this scale.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 2-4 (2 configs × 100 steps, each ~1-2 GPU hours on RTX 4090)

verdicts.target: TOTAL_COMPUTE zero_gap: WSD schedule + critical-batch-size batch ramp
verdicts.reason: Field candidate from arXiv:2505.23971 (OLMo: 43% step savings) and arXiv:2404.06395 (MiniCPM basis). Documented in docs/research/gpu-math-multiplier-table-v2-2026-06-11.json but no measurement receipt at ember scale. Pure schedule change (zero code cost), field-sourced, testable via direct comparison.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run two 286-step rung-0 or rung-1 trainings: Treatment A with baseline schedule (current), Treatment B with WSD (warmup-stable-decay) + critical-batch-size ramp per field papers. Freeze all other hyperparams.
decisive_experiment.measurement: For each: loss_100, loss_200, FLOPs per step, steps-to-target-loss (if target known). Primary: does Treatment B achieve target-loss in ≤172 steps (43% fewer than 286)? Secondary: is loss trajectory stable under WSD?
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if Treatment B requires >260 steps to match Treatment A's loss_100 (fails field's 43% savings claim), or if loss shows oscillation/instability under WSD+batch-ramp.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 3-5 (2 configs × 286 steps ≈ 3-4 GPU hours each)

verdicts.target: TOTAL_COMPUTE zero_gap: Kernel-level fusion beyond fused-Muon (liger-fused cross-entropy, FP8 quantized forward)
verdicts.reason: Fused-Muon measured 1.3459x speedup (PR #188, receipted). Liger-fused cross-entropy and FP8 quantized forward identified as candidates but not receipted at rung-2 scale. Both are real, field-standard implementations. Sequential ablation feasible.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run 100-step rung-1 trainings (1.2B params) in sequence: Baseline (current fused-Muon), +liger-fused-cross-entropy, +FP8-quantized-forward (with unit-scaling guards from arXiv:2502.05967). Measure each independently and combined.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Wall-clock time per step, FLOPs per step, peak VRAM, loss convergence curve. Calculate speedup: (baseline_time / treatment_time). Check loss matches baseline within 1e-4 (numerical stability).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if any fusion kernel: (a) causes NaN/inf in loss, (b) yields <1.05x wall-clock speedup, or (c) shows combined effect <1.10x (fails to justify integration complexity).
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 3-5 (1 baseline + 3 treatments × 100 steps ≈ 1-2 GPU hours each)

verdicts.target: TRAINING_INSTABILITY_AT_SCALE zero_gap: QK-norm tuning at scale
verdicts.reason: Documented in docs/research/gemma4-unified-architecture.md but no ablation receipt at rung-2+ scale. It's cited as important (part of the unified architecture) yet its effect size is unmeasured. Could be vestigial or critical—only ablation will tell.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run 150-step rung-2 training (1.9B params, burn-in + stability window): Treatment A with QK-norm enabled (current), Treatment B with QK-norm disabled (set to 1.0). Same config otherwise.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Loss trajectory, NaN/inf occurrence rate, divergence distance (max_loss - expected_trend). Record every 10 steps.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if Treatment B remains stable (no NaN, loss within 5% of Treatment A)—indicating QK-norm is vestigial. Verdict survives if Treatment B diverges, NaNs, or drifts >10% loss—indicating QK-norm is load-bearing.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 2-3 (early divergence likely, 150 steps ≈ 1-1.5 GPU hours per config)

verdicts.target: TRAINING_INSTABILITY_AT_SCALE zero_gap: z-loss tuning at scale
verdicts.reason: Formula published (10⁻⁵·log²Z on final softmax) as required at 7B+, but no ablation receipt at rung-1 or rung-2 (1.2B–1.9B). Effect at intermediate scales unknown. Untested at ember's current range.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run 150-step rung-2 training (1.9B params): Treatment A with z-loss enabled (factor = 10⁻⁵·log²Z), Treatment B with z-loss disabled (factor = 1.0). Match all other hyperparams.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Max logit magnitude per step, loss NaN rate, divergence distance. Record max_logit every 10 steps.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if Treatment B stays stable (no NaN, max_logit <100)—indicating z-loss is unnecessary at rung-2. Verdict survives if Treatment B shows runaway logits (>200) or NaN—indicating z-loss is stability-critical.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 2-3 (early NaN likely, ≈1-1.5 GPU hours per config)

verdicts.target: TRAINING_INSTABILITY_AT_SCALE zero_gap: Per-step loss divergence halt mechanism
verdicts.reason: Step traces are now recorded (#686). Automation is missing: v8/v9 rely on manual kill-band thresholds. This is a clear low-cost automation opportunity. Predicates are standard (loss gradient > threshold, divergence distance > N sigma). Integration cost is zero GPU hours.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Retro-fit automated divergence predicate on existing v8/v9 step traces: divergence_distance(t) = max_loss(t-10:t) - predicted_trend(t). Define kill_threshold = 3 * sigma(recent_divergences). Pre-register threshold BEFORE examining v8/v9 data.
decisive_experiment.measurement: On v8/v9 traces, compute F1 score: (True Positives) / (True Positives + False Positives + False Negatives). Ground truth = manual kills actually issued by operator. Check: does predicate catch >95% of manual-kill cases? False positive rate <5%?
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if F1 <0.85 or false positive rate >10%—indicating predicate is not reliable enough to replace manual review. Verdict survives if F1 ≥0.90 and false-positive rate ≤5%.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 1-2 (pure analysis on existing traces, no GPU)

verdicts.target: TRAINING_INSTABILITY_AT_SCALE zero_gap: Coupling constants (QK-norm ↔ z-loss ↔ dropout ↔ batch-size)
verdicts.reason: Recipes are frozen per issue #121 (W1 acceptance), but interaction effects are unquantified. The frozen values may be stable at rung-2 but could require re-tuning at rung-3+. Field evidence (OLMo, others) suggests some coupling (e.g., batch-size ↔ LR). A cheap sensitivity analysis would validate scaling assumptions.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Design a reduced-scope sensitivity sweep on rung-1 (100-step runs): hold baseline (QK-norm=X, z-loss=Y, dropout=Z, batch_size=B), then perturb ONE hyperparameter ±20% (e.g., QK-norm → 0.8X, 1.2X). Run 3 seed replicates per condition.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Loss trajectory and max divergence distance. For each perturbation, compute: mean_loss_delta = mean(loss_perturbation - loss_baseline) and sigma. Focus on: does any single perturbation change mean loss >5%? Do pairs of perturbations interact (non-additive)?
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if all perturbations ±20% show <1% loss change—indicating frozen recipes are robust. Verdict survives if any perturbation alters loss >3% or pairs show interaction >additive—indicating coupling needs characterization before rung-3.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 4-6 (baseline + 8 perturbations × 3 seeds × 100 steps ≈ ~5 GPU hours)

verdicts.target: TRAINING_INSTABILITY_AT_SCALE field_lever: NF4 + stochastic-rounding optimizer states (SR4-MASTER, P3)
verdicts.reason: NF4 is real (Dettmers et al., bitsandbytes). Stochastic rounding is standard ML. Combining them for optimizer states is a plausible but unvalidated hypothesis. The audit's '100x grid-vs-update gap' is speculative (unreceipted in field literature). Cost is low (~368M model footprint). Queued and ready to attempt.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run 100-step rung-1 trainings (1.2B params): Treatment A (baseline, fp32 optimizer states), Treatment B (NF4 weight matrices only, fp32 momentum/variance), Treatment C (NF4 weight matrices + stochastic-rounding on grad aggregation). Hold training loop identical otherwise.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Loss trajectory, parameter sign-flip rate per 10 steps, peak VRAM used. Primary: does loss_100_C ≈ loss_100_A (convergence match)? Secondary: is flip-rate stable in Treatment C? Peak VRAM <baseline + 368MB?
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Verdict kills if Treatment C shows >5% loss divergence from baseline, flip-rate stalling (slope <-0.01 per 10 steps), or memory overhead >500MB. Verdict survives if C matches baseline loss within 2%, flip-rate smooth, memory overhead ≤368MB.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: gpu-hours-post-run: 2-3 (3 configs × 100 steps ≈ 1 GPU hour per config)
